scope: DCP-LETT-1481 P1 cross-correspondent Müller acknowledgement probe

evidence.quote: I have had a short letter from Müller of Berlin, expressing interest in my Book
evidence.assessment: Darwin reports a short letter from an unnamed Müller of Berlin as encouragement about his Cirripedia book; P1 does not give Müller’s forename, date, or letter text.

preserved_candidates.title: To Johannes Peter Müller 10 February [1849]
preserved_candidates.assessment: This is the only preserved Johannes Peter Müller record located. It is Darwin’s outgoing 1849 request for Alepas and other cirripede specimens, addressed to Professor J. Müller at Berlin. Its body contains no incoming Müller prose and predates the 8 May 1852 acknowledgement by more than three years; it cannot identify the reported short letter.

preserved_candidates.title: To Hermann Müller [before 5 May 1872]
preserved_candidates.source_sha256: not used as a period candidate
preserved_candidates.assessment: A later Darwin-to-Hermann Müller record, outside the relevant period and a different Müller, not the reported 1852 source.

finding: No preserved incoming Johannes Peter Müller letter matching Darwin’s P1 acknowledgement was located in the searched all_letters projection. The available JP Müller record is Darwin’s 10 February 1849 outgoing specimen request, not an incoming response. Darwin’s wording establishes his awareness of a short Berlin letter and its supportive content, but does not establish its exact date, dispatch, receipt route, or surviving text.
relationship_status: knowledge_witness_only; no incoming endpoint and no direct reply pair identified
retrieval_limit: Further identification would require an external/archive source request; no network retrieval was made.
notes: DCP-LETT-1481 was read fully with XML date attributes, body, exclusions, scholarly sections, footnotes and bibliography.
DCP-LETT-1224 was read fully with its XML date, author/recipient roles, apparatus and bibliography.
Other Müller records located were Hermann Müller or unrelated later material; they were not promoted to Johannes Peter Müller.
The 1849 outgoing JP Müller letter may explain the correspondence relationship but cannot prove the identity of the 1852 incoming acknowledgement.
